video_goal: Demonstrate the complete process of boiling, cooling, and peeling a chicken egg.
required_subjects_and_props: Raw brown chicken egg, small metal saucepan, water, stove, metal slotted spoon, digital kitchen timer, glass bowl, ice cubes, wooden cutting board, knife

outline_steps.visual_action: Pour clear water from a glass pitcher into a small metal saucepan resting on a stovetop burner.
A hand turns the stove dial clockwise to the 'High' position.
The water inside the metal saucepan reaches a rolling boil, with large bubbles rapidly breaking the surface.
A hand carefully places a raw brown chicken egg onto the center of a metal slotted spoon.
The hand gently lowers the slotted spoon to submerge the brown chicken egg completely into the boiling water, then pulls the empty spoon away.
An index finger presses the 'Start' button on a digital kitchen timer that displays '07:00'.
The brown egg vibrates and rolls slightly amidst the vigorously boiling water bubbles in the saucepan.
A hand drops a handful of ice cubes into a clear glass bowl filled with cold water to create an ice bath.
The digital kitchen timer display flashes '00:00' as the countdown finishes.
A hand uses the metal slotted spoon to scoop the boiled brown egg out of the bubbling water.
The slotted spoon lowers the hot egg directly into the glass bowl of ice water, leaving it to rest among the ice cubes.
A hand lifts the cooled egg from the ice bath and taps it firmly against a wooden cutting board to fracture the shell.
Two thumbs peel away the fractured brown shell and inner membrane to reveal the smooth, white cooked egg underneath.
A sharp knife slices the peeled white egg in half, separating the two halves to show a firm, bright yellow cooked yolk.
